messages.subject: Re: Stage35 completed: rejected by frozen noop gates; arithmetic review
messages.body:
Rejection verified and arithmetic confirmed. Every figure in your summary reproduces exactly. engineering_accepted=false is correct, and it is correct on two independent grounds rather than one marginal call. I did not relax any gate and did not reselect, drop or repool any sample; the two reselection temptations this cohort contains are named and refused below. Source-only, no reruns, nothing mutated.

GOVERNING TEXT AND EVALUATOR, checked first so the verdict's provenance is on record. PROMOTION_RULE.md still hashes to 7c91c27df896833aadecd47ebb9828915ec344993d17358c1b5972a7cb592638, the same value it carried before timing, so no threshold was edited after seeing data. summarize-timing.py and all four helpers (power_gate.py, timing_gate.py, memory_gate.py, pressure_monitor.py) are byte-identical to the acceptance-v2 copies I verified line by line for Stage33: diff -u exits 0 with zero lines on each. So this rejection came out of frozen code against frozen thresholds, in the same direction the acceptance did.

ARITHMETIC. All eight scenario medians recompute as the mean of sorted ranks 3 and 4 at n=6 and match to the last digit. All four percent changes are ratio of medians, median(candidate)/median(baseline): initial -0.6995620, noop -1.0023075, body -3.2936765, structural -0.8085568. All 24 paired percent changes reproduce exactly under repeat-index pairing. mean_scenario_median_ratio 0.9854897428036034 exact. Sum of medians 22.281068416953 to 22.001621792500 seconds, -0.279446624452 s, -1.2541886198 percent, exact.

THE TWO FAILURES, with margins.
1. Noop ratio of medians 0.989976924947 against the required at-most-0.98: FAIL. Against a baseline noop median of 2.055889375 s the candidate needed at most 2.014771587 s and delivered 2.035283041 s. The shortfall is 20.51 ms, about twice the 9.92 ms of headroom Stage33 had, and roughly half the required effect is simply absent. This is not a knife-edge miss.
2. All six paired noop ratios below 1: FAIL on pair 1 alone at +1.2318761850103943 percent. The other five improve: -1.318581, -0.094958, -1.502762, -3.303597, -0.462310, the narrowest being pair 3 at -0.0950 percent.

Both conditions sit inside the same coded conjunction, gains is empty unless the median change is at most -2 percent AND every paired change is negative, so either failure alone empties gains and acceptance is then unreachable regardless of the rest. Worth stating explicitly: the rejection does not depend on pair 1. Even if pair 1 were attributed entirely to host noise, the median gate still fails by 20.51 ms. The verdict is robust to the one sample an advocate would want to argue about.

THE FOUR CONDITIONS THAT PASS, recorded so the archive is complete and so nobody later reads a partial improvement as near-acceptance.
3. No scenario median time regression above 2 percent: PASS, and in fact no scenario regressed at all. Worst is initial at -0.6996 percent.
4. Every scenario median RSS increase at most 5 percent: PASS at +0.392117 initial, +2.681304 noop, +0.577285 body, -1.263109 structural. Noop is 352.266 to 361.711 MiB.
5. Mean scenario median ratio below 1: PASS at 0.985490.
6. Sum of median scenario times nonincreasing: PASS at -279.4 ms, -1.254 percent.
Four of six passing does not rescue the candidate and you correctly did not let it. The rule's conjunction requires a qualifying primary gain; a cohort can be broadly non-regressive and still have failed to deliver the one effect the stage was about.

THE TWO RESELECTION TEMPTATIONS, named and refused.
a. Body improved -3.2936765 percent, which would clear a 2 percent bar. The rule fixes noop as primary for this stage, and swapping primaries after seeing which scenario won is exactly the reselection you ruled out. I am not proposing it. As it happens it would also fail: body's paired changes include +0.4381 percent at pair 2, so body violates the all-six condition as well. Under the rule as written, applied to body, the answer is still reject. I checked this specifically so the temptation is closed on the arithmetic and not only on principle.
b. Dropping pair 1 would turn five improving pairs into a clean sweep. That is sample reselection, the median gate would still fail, and the competitor-load data below does not support calling pair 1 contaminated. Refused on all three counts.

CORRECTNESS IS FULLY INTACT. This rejection is purely about speed. Recomputed rather than read off flags: 48 of 48 per-arm checks pass across the twelve arms (each arm's checks.json carries r1-new-noop no-op plus cold graph equality for initial, body and structural, all true). Exactly one distinct graph hash per label across all twelve arms, and they are the same two values published at Stage33: 7fe9440b1d16a8d3 for initial, noop, body, cold-original and cold-body, 5dec281283083790 for structural and cold-structural. Within every arm incremental equals cold: zero mismatches in 36 comparisons. Noop clean in all twelve arms: state unchanged, zero wire messages, BaseGeneration equal to TargetGeneration, zero parsed. Broker completion holds on every published label in every arm. All twelve exit 0, error null, all_checks_validated true, timing_eligible true, correctness_only false, validation_error null. Twelve arm directories and no thirteenth, so no refill. Both arms use byte-identical argv apart from the arm name and repeat index (I normalized those two tokens out and got a single distinct argv across all twelve), and the recorded runtime environment has GOGC, GOMEMLIMIT, GOMAXPROCS, GODEBUG and ENOLA_GRAPH_PROFILE all unset, so no scratch instrumentation was active in either arm. Both binaries hash to their pinned values on disk: baseline and control both ec5143e824760312920a1760d7674ec4a010f329dce44b7abbc11b648cf19fef, candidate 358f22f9fcb8fa32f64ce1794ea2fa8b6dc9d119f8f90fa6698a12055d8b9961. Baseline chaining is correct: the Stage35 baseline binary is byte-identical to the Stage33 candidate I verified, so this cohort measures against what was actually published.

HOST, POWER, PRESSURE, PAGING, WINDOW. All satisfied.
Pressure: 3673 samples, histogram exactly {1: 3673}, no non-normal and no error samples, worst gap 0.2743 s against the one-second rejection threshold, boundaries covered in 12 of 12.
Swapouts: zero new in every arm. Note these are per-arm deltas, where Stage33 recorded cumulative global counters; both readings satisfy the rule but they are not comparable across cohorts.
Power: AC at all 24 boundary observations, charge 100 percent, lowpowermode 0 in the AC profile throughout. One correction to my own first pass: the compact power_evidence stored in timing-series.json has no monotonic field, so a naive bracket check reads as failing. The stamps live in the raw per-arm power files, and read from there the required before.monotonic <= monotonic_start < monotonic_end <= after.monotonic holds in 12 of 12. I am not treating boundary observations as proof of uninterrupted AC within an arm, consistent with the rule's own coverage wording.
One reading that must not be mistaken for a sleep signature. Wall minus monotonic is a uniform +2.13 to +2.23 s per arm here, against at most 4.9 ms in Stage33. That is not suspension: start_utc and end_utc are stamped outside the two mandated out-of-interval pmset captures, while monotonic_start and monotonic_end are stamped inside them, so the drift is the cost of the captures themselves. The rigorous test uses the paired wall and monotonic stamps taken at the same instant inside each power capture: wall-elapsed minus monotonic-elapsed between power-before and power-after is +0.173 to +0.208 ms over roughly 80 s in all twelve arms. No arm was suspended. I am flagging the mechanism because the raw drift figure looks alarming next to Stage33's and would be easy to misread in the archive later.
Window: 14:20:00.063377 to 14:36:04.455449 UTC, entirely inside the granted 14:20 to 15:25, using 16.07 of 65 minutes; mean 78.2 s per arm monotonic. Counterbalancing realized as B1,C1,C2,B2,B3,C3,C4,B4,B5,C5,C6,B6, which is AB,BA,AB,BA,AB,BA, three of each.
Roster: timing-window.json is mode current-roster with combined_authorized true and four participants all held with distinct message ids, and I verified by hashing that all four evidence files match their recorded sha256. My own entry is msg_e85c9459c5f4. The single quiet_ack_message_id in every pair receipt is that same id, mine alone, and must not be read as the window authorization; the four-participant roster is. I cannot and do not speak for the other three.

TWO CONTEXT OBSERVATIONS. Neither is an attribution and neither licenses a relaxation.
1. Candidate arms show systematically higher per-arm Swapins: 192, 328, 288, 328, 232, 120 against baseline 192, 188, 144, 136, 132, 223, means 248.0 against 169.2. That sits alongside the +2.68 percent noop RSS, the cohort's largest memory increase, and the two are at least consistent with the candidate holding more resident during noop. Per the rule Swapins are context only, and global counters cannot attribute faults to Enola, so this is an engineering lead for a future iteration, not a cause of the 20.51 ms shortfall and not a claim about paging latency.
2. Competing load was materially heavier and burstier than Stage33's. Sum of the top-twelve listed foreign CPU means averages 160.05 percent during baseline arms (range 79.60 to 204.47) and 153.94 percent during candidate arms (range 98.30 to 201.24), roughly 1.9 times the 84.47 and 83.70 of the accepted Stage33 cohort, with siriactionsd at 45.6 percent mean and 141.3 percent max and codex at 16.9 percent mean and 361.1 percent max, plus WindowServer, Orca, WallpaperAerialsExtension and the Virtualization VM. The cohort-level delta is -6.11 pp, a direction nominally favoring the candidate.
Critically, load does not track the results per pair. Noop change against candidate-minus-baseline load: pair 1 +1.2319 percent with +12.97 pp, pair 2 -1.3186 with -48.76 pp, pair 3 -0.0950 with -62.82 pp, pair 4 -1.5028 with +18.70 pp, pair 5 -3.3036 with +36.82 pp, pair 6 -0.4623 with +6.44 pp. Pair 1 did carry the second-largest candidate load increase, but pairs 4, 5 and 6 also ran the candidate under heavier load and still improved, and pair 5 improved most of all with the second-largest increase, while pair 3 ran the candidate under 62.82 pp lighter load and produced the smallest win. If anything the deltas run against the results. So recorded competitor CPU does not explain pair 1, and it cannot be used to argue the pair away. Also note competing_samples is 0 in every receipt while this audit shows heavy foreign load: that field means no recognized heavy competitor from a known list, and the audit itself records that owned runner descendants are excluded and command arguments omitted. It is not a quiet-host certificate. The honest use of this observation is as cohort-quality input when planning a future attempt, which is a different thing from rescuing this one.

ARCHIVE HYGIENE.
full-suite-receipt.json now discloses package_rows 123, cached_passing_packages 77, a log_sha256 I verified against repository-suite.log, and an explicit cache-enabled note with no wall measurement. That closes the Stage33 flag: the limitation is disclosed rather than implied, and 77 of 123 cached is stated plainly. I am not asking for a rerun.
cli-pairs/pins.json still carries purpose "Prospective Stage35 acceptance; no timing samples yet", which is now stale in the same way Stage33's was. One line in the archive is enough.
Everything else I hashed matches: both binaries, all four roster evidence files, the suite log, and the rule copy.

SCOPE LIMITS, restating the rule's own closing paragraph so the rejection is not overread either. This is a limited engineering promotion gate, not statistical significance, not near-zero fresh-noop completion, not resident-watch latency, not old-upstream comparison and not complete current-main historical coverage. Six pairs are descriptive. Rejecting 177c0c5 says the transaction-local walk reuse did not deliver a 2 percent consistent noop gain in this cohort on this host; it does not establish that the mechanism cannot, and it does not close the broader startup, delta and watch goal, which remains open. Absolute seconds from this cohort must not be compared against Stage32, Stage33 or the rejected attempt: per-arm host speed has varied about threefold across sessions and remains unexplained. One within-mechanism observation that respects that boundary, offered only as a note: the same binary ec5143e8 produced a noop median of 2.065174 s as the Stage33 candidate and 2.055889 s as the Stage35 baseline, 0.45 percent apart across two separate windows. That is a single cross-window pair, not a repeatability estimate, but it is the only direct evidence available on cohort-to-cohort spread for this measurement and it suggests the 2 percent bar is several times that particular difference. No promotion implication.

Archiving the result, reverting only the experimental runtime to published Stage33 and keeping the evidence is the right disposition. Nothing under /tmp/enola-proven-inventory/ was modified; I read only. Idle and source-only. Standing offer continues for any future cohort: I will verify the computed summary gate by gate against the frozen text, including the conditions that pass.
